themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints surged to 16 this week—a 184% increase over the 8-week average of 5.6 per week—signaling a rapid pest control crisis affecting residential areas in Kingsbridge/Bedford Park.
evidence: 16 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.62)
184% spike in a single week suggests acute infestation event or systemic sanitation breakdown
Converges with 1,274 unsanitary condition complaints (90-day volume), indicating broader neighborhood conditions
reporting_angles: Ground-level reporting: interview residents in buildings with confirmed infestations; map complaint clusters by block
City response: did DOHMH issue emergency pest control orders? What's the typical response time in this district?

themes_detail.label: Construction Site Safety Failures
themes_detail.summary: Building/Environmental Site Safety (BEST) complaints exploded to 3 this week—a 1100% spike from a near-zero 8-week baseline—indicating potential ongoing construction hazards in the district.
evidence: 3 BEST/Site Safety complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, severity: high)
1100% spike from essentially zero baseline; extremely rare complaints becoming suddenly common
363 DOB building permits filed in 90 days (221 alterations, 102 new buildings) indicate active construction footprint
reporting_angles: Identify which specific sites generated the three complaints; cross-reference with active DOB permits and recent violations
Interview DOB inspectors and construction safety advocates about enforcement capacity in this district

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints skyrocketed to 60 last week—a 515% increase over the 8-week average of 9.8 per week (z-score: 17.3)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, suggesting a new source of sustained disruption.
evidence: 60 commercial noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 9.8 weekly average over 8 weeks (515% spike, z-score: 17.3)
Highest z-score in entire dataset (17.3 vs next highest 8.14); extremely rare statistical event
Residential noise also elevated at 2,590 total over 90 days, suggesting noise is district-wide problem
reporting_angles: Map which neighborhoods/intersections generated the spike; identify new bars, restaurants, music venues, or construction sites that opened recently
Investigate: did NYPD increase enforcement, or are complaints being filed at higher rate due to resident frustration?

themes_detail.label: Lead Exposure Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints quadrupled to 6 last week—a 300% increase over the 8-week average of 1.5 per week—flagging potential lead paint or water contamination in a neighborhood with aging housing stock.
evidence: 6 lead complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 4.5)
Paint/plaster complaints also elevated at 868 total over 90 days; suggests deteriorating building conditions
Consistent budget request for DEP capital (water systems) indicates district-known infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings/blocks generated lead complaints; cross-reference with HPD violation history and DOE school proximity
Public health angle: are children's lead levels being tested? What's the city's response protocol?

themes_detail.label: Plumbing and Water System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints increased 58% to 109 last week (vs. 68.8 weekly average), and water system complaints jumped 127% to 40 last week (vs. 17.6 average)—a converging infrastructure crisis affecting basic utilities in 363 active construction sites.
evidence: Plumbing complaints UP 58% last week (109 vs. 68.8 average, z-score: 8.14)
Water system complaints UP 127% last week (40 vs. 17.6 average, z-score: 3.47)
Combined 149 complaints for two related utilities; 4,191 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days suggest systemic heating/water delivery problems
reporting_angles: Are these complaints concentrated in buildings managed by specific landlords or in specific neighborhoods?
DEP infrastructure audit: are water mains aging? Is there excavation-related damage from the 363 active construction permits?
